Whelp is backed by 500 Global. No public developer API or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Customer Database
providers.description: Customer Database is the topic dedicated to APIs, schemas, vocabularies, and reference designs for the systems of record that store customer identity, profile, contact, preference, consent, and account data. A customer database underpins CRM, marketing automation, customer data platforms (CDPs), customer service, billing, and analytics use cases, and is increasingly expected to support API-first access, schema-on-write data quality, real-time eventing, GDPR/CCPA consent and erasure workflows, and identity resolution across web, mobile, and offline channels. This repository tracks the vendors, standards, and patterns that make customer data accessible, governed, and portable.

providers.name: Mosaic
providers.description: Mosaic is a North American brand experience agency with global reach, and one of the pillar agencies of Acosta Group. It works across four service lines — experiential marketing, B2B corporate experiences and events, integrated commerce and shopper programs, and field sales and marketing — plus third-party labor, assisted selling, retail merchandising, sales training, retail execution and surge staffing for retail, B2B and CPG environments. With roots in Toronto and Dallas and offices in Jacksonville, Mosaic says it has spent more than 35 years building brand experiences designed to drive awareness, engagement, conversion and behaviour change. Mosaic publishes no developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Tillpoint
providers.description: Tillpoint is a modular, cloud-based EPOS (electronic point of sale) and business management platform for retail, hospitality, and services. A single subscription bundles 25+ modules - Point of Sale, Inventory, Customers/CRM, Staff, Accounting, Purchase Orders, Reporting, and more - across one terminal or thousands of locations. As of this review Tillpoint does not publish a documented public or partner developer API - there is no developer portal, no API reference, and no OpenAPI. Connectivity is delivered through pre-built integrations (QuickBooks Online, Xero, WooCommerce, PayPal, Worldpay, Mailchimp). The API surfaces catalogued here (Point of Sale, Inventory, Customers, Accounting) are logical capability areas of the platform and are honestly marked as endpointsModeled - no endpoints are fabricated. Direct/programmatic access requires contacting Tillpoint.

providers.name: TravelJoy
providers.description: TravelJoy is software for travel advisors and agencies — a client CRM, itinerary and proposal builder, secure payment collection, forms and questionnaires, and automated client communication combined in one platform. Travel professionals use it to manage trips, capture and nurture leads, send branded proposals, gather traveler details, and collect payments. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass TravelJoy publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK program; this profile tracks its identity and public web properties for discovery.

providers.name: Paperplane
providers.description: Paperplane is an AI sales-productivity tool (Y Combinator W23, backed by Bloomberg Beta) that automatically takes notes on sales calls and keeps a rep's CRM up to date. It connects to a team's calendar and to conversational intelligence and call-recording tools such as Gong and Chorus, transcribes and analyzes each call, then writes the results back to Salesforce — updating opportunity fields, notes, and action items so sales teams spend less time on manual CRM data entry and stay on top of their deals. The product is organized around opportunities, calls, and notes, with integrations for Google Calendar, Gong, Chorus, and Salesforce. Paperplane appears to have wound down: Y Combinator lists the company as Inactive (and now describes it as a credit risk management platform for builders' merchants, so it pivoted at least once before stopping), its marketing site presents no TLS certificate, its application host returns a Vercel 402 DEPLOYMENT_DISABLED, and its API host is an Envoy ingress that 404s every path with an empty body. Two surfaces remain live: a GitBook documentation site — which is an unfilled starter template carrying GitBook's own placeholder copy, last updated three years ago — with an llms.txt index, and a Clerk-hosted OpenID Connect identity instance at clerk.paperplane.ai that still serves real OIDC and RFC 8414 discovery documents. There is no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, MCP server, or agent card.

providers.name: HELP
providers.description: This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-linked lead of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The website pointer on this record resolves to Venturz (operated by GoVenturz, LLC), an all-in-one business operating system for founders that bundles 15+ tools — website builder, CRM, email marketing, payments, and analytics — behind a single dashboard alongside an "AI co-founder" assistant, a founder community, a startup academy, and Venturz Capital funding. As of this enrichment pass Venturz publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface, so no machine-readable API artifacts could be harvested. See x-identity-note regarding the stub name versus the linked brand.

providers.name: EZLynx
providers.description: EZLynx is an insurance agency platform combining real-time comparative rating, an agency management system (AMS), and CRM for independent property and casualty (P&C) insurance agencies. Part of Applied Systems since 2021, EZLynx offers enterprise API solutions that let agencies push and pull data, create and update applicants, contacts, prospects, and opportunities, create policy headers, retrieve policy and quote-result data, and drive high-volume automated quoting through the EZLynx Rating Engine and Quoting Automation Services (QAS). An event-driven layer emits webhooks in XML or JSON for platform changes. API access is partner and enterprise-gated (contact sales, OAuth 2.0), not a public self-serve developer program, so the API surface below is honestly modeled from EZLynx's public product and integration material rather than a published open reference.

providers.name: Pico
providers.description: Pico was a creator-monetization and CRM platform for online creators, publishers, and media companies, built in New York and backed by Bloomberg Beta. It combined an audience CRM with email capture, landing pages, paywalls, memberships, and subscription payments in a single tool so creators could identify their audience, gate premium content, and convert readers into paying members. Pico raised a $6.5M round in 2021 ("Pico 2.0") and a $10M Series A in 2023, when it rebranded to Hype (hype.co) and refocused on link-in-bio, lead generation, and growth tools for creators, gyms, coaches, and athletes. In February 2026 Hype was acquired by MMA.inc and the product was wound down. The developer API — authenticated with an X-Api-Key header and documented at docs.trypico.com — is retired: the API host api.trypico.com no longer resolves, the reference bucket has been deleted, and hype.co now serves only an acquisition notice directing users to support@hype.co.

providers.name: Housewhisper
providers.description: HouseWhisper (legal name Real Estate Productivity, Inc.) is a Seattle-based AI platform for real estate teams and brokerages, founded by former Zillow executives. It acts as a 24/7 AI teammate that automates the full lead lifecycle through personalized voice and text conversations: a Lead Engine that re-engages and revives cold database contacts, a Rules Engine that routes leads to the right agent with fallback escalations, and an AI Teammate that handles CRM updates, follow-ups, scheduling, reminders, and administrative busywork by call or text. It connects to real estate CRM, dialer, and calendar systems via API keys with no data migration, integrating with Follow Up Boss, Sierra Interactive, kvCORE, MoxiWorks, Salesforce, Lofty, HubSpot, and others. Pricing is outcome-based (a small monthly platform fee plus referral fees on closed deals). HouseWhisper has raised roughly $10M in seed funding led by Mayfield. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Tungee
providers.description: Tungee (Guangzhou Tungee Technology Co., Ltd., 探迹科技) is a Chinese AI sales-intelligence company backed by Qiming Venture Partners. Its Tungee AI Sales Cloud covers the full B2B sales cycle -- AI prospecting over a 300M+ company knowledge graph, inbound capture, outreach via call center, SMS, and email, and an AI CRM -- plus a Sales GPT agent line, a mobile app, and a DingTalk edition. The group also operates Futern, an international B2B leads product, and reports 50,000+ customers. Tungee publishes no public developer portal or API documentation.

providers.name: Humanitru
providers.description: Humanitru is an integration-first CRM and fundraising platform built for nonprofits, museums, zoos, aquariums, botanic gardens, and food banks. Rather than forcing organizations into an all-in-one ecosystem, Humanitru consolidates donor, membership, ticketing, email marketing, accounting, and volunteer data from more than 40 partner tools into a single 360-degree view, then layers automated insights, reporting, and donor-engagement workflows on top. The company positions itself around data consolidation and retention, citing customer outcomes such as increased active donors and improved donor retention, and pairs the platform with one-on-one support staffed by former fundraisers and database managers. Humanitru (formerly operating as Totem Insights) is a Techstars portfolio company. It exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or documentation; all connectivity is delivered through its curated native integration catalog.

providers.name: Roofr
providers.description: Roofr is an all-in-one roofing software and CRM built for roofing contractors, bundling aerial roof measurement reports, an instant online estimator, digital proposals with e-signature, integrated payments, material ordering, a job calendar, and pipeline/CRM tooling into one platform to help roofers win, run, and close jobs. Roofr does not publish a public developer API or self-serve documentation: the only API key it issues (under Settings and Integrations) exists to connect Roofr to Zapier, and any broader programmatic access is sales-gated behind a demo. Automation for external systems is delivered primarily through Zapier triggers (new Instant Estimator lead, proposal signed, proposal marked lost) rather than a documented REST API. Roofr is a portfolio company of Bullpen Capital.

providers.name: Aisle Planner
providers.description: Aisle Planner is a cloud-based business management platform for wedding and event professionals - planners, venues, caterers, florists, and photographers - bundling lead management, proposals/contracts with e-signatures, invoicing and online payments, timelines, budgets, guest and vendor management, seating charts, event websites, and online RSVP into one system. Aisle Planner does NOT publish a public, self-service developer API. There is no developer portal, no public API reference, and no OpenAPI definition. The only "API key" Aisle Planner issues is a private per-account key found in Business Settings that plugs into a single pre-built Zapier integration - triggers are new project, new lead, and payment received; actions are create wedding project, create event project, and create lead - it is not a general-purpose, self-serve REST API a third-party developer can register for and call directly.

providers.name: Panora
providers.description: Panora is an open-source unified API platform that allows developers to integrate with hundreds of third-party tools through a single API. It provides a unified interface for CRM, HR, accounting, and other integrations.

providers.name: Chasi
providers.description: Chasi (Chasi AI) is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company building an AI revenue engine for the equipment industry — sales, rental, and service. Chasi deploys AI agents that plug into an equipment dealer or rental company's existing stack and work around the clock to handle lead intake, quoting, CRM updates, follow-ups, and booking coordination, so teams respond faster, sell more, and maximize fleet utilization without adding headcount. Founded in 2025 by Akash Pavan and Sarman Aulakh, the company targets an industry where fleet utilization often sits below 60% and reps lose hours each day to email, voicemail, and manual data entry. Chasi ships a Clerk-authenticated tenant application at app.chasi.ai, a first-party iOS app, an interactive demo, a Rootly-hosted status page, and a trust center, and is live with equipment businesses in the US and Europe — but as of August 2026 it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP server, agent card, or SDK, and its go-to-market is sales-led through a booked demo and a 90-day pilot.

providers.name: Marand
providers.description: Marand Software (Marand d.o.o., Ljubljana, Slovenia) builds cloud-native Business Support System components for communications service providers, positioned as a vendor of TM Forum Open Digital Architecture (ODA) components. Its product line covers a Unified Product Catalog, 360 Customer / Inventory, CPQ, CRM, Multiservice Enterprise Billing, AI/ML solutions and custom software services. Marand's components implement the TM Forum Information Framework (SID) and expose TM Forum Open APIs; the company is a TM Forum Open API Gold certified member, holds Open API conformance certifications for TMF633 (Service Catalog Management, 2022) and TMF673 (Geographic Address Management, 2023), achieved "Ready for ODA" status in March 2024, and co-authored the TMF760 Product Configuration API with Orange and Amdocs as one of the first fifth-generation TM Forum Open APIs. Marand publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification of its own — its APIs ship inside licensed components deployed at operator customers, and the contracts they implement are the TM Forum specifications.

providers.name: Ciro
providers.description: Ciro (Ciro Technologies Inc.) is an AI sales platform that finds a revenue team's best accounts, deeply qualifies each contact, runs a contact data waterfall for verified emails and phone numbers, and writes signal-based outbound that is pushed directly into existing sales tools. Reps command Ciro in plain English from Slack, where it runs prospect searches, enriches contacts, queries the CRM, analyzes CSVs, drafts multi-step personalized email sequences, and recommends the highest-ROI campaigns. It integrates with Salesforce and HubSpot (CRM); Salesloft, Outreach, Gong Engage, and Instantly (sales engagement); Slack; and webhook-based export to Clay and Zapier. Ciro is sold through a sales-led motion with no published pricing, is SOC 2 Type II certified, and was backed by Y Combinator and CRV. On 2026-07-08 Reevo announced it had acquired Ciro and is folding the prospecting agent into its revenue operating system; ciro.io remains live and still sells, and every page now carries an "acquired by Reevo" banner. Ciro was surfaced as a portfolio company of CRV and enriched into the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public developer API, no developer documentation, no OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP or AsyncAPI contract, no SDK in any package registry, and no /.well-known/ document — every one of those was probed on 2026-08-14 and missed.

providers.name: Loft
providers.description: Loft is a Brazilian real estate technology (proptech) company founded in 2018 and headquartered in Sao Paulo. It operates a marketplace for buying, selling, and renting residential property alongside a broad platform of software and financial services for the real estate sector, including a CRM and property-management tools for agencies, digital proposals and e-signatures, lead generation, rental administration, and fintech products such as rental guarantees (Fianca Aluguel), home financing, credit with property collateral, and residential and commercial insurance. Backed by a16z, QED Investors, Fifth Wall, D1 Capital, Thrive Capital, and Baillie Gifford, Loft is a market leader in Brazil's real estate fintech space. Loft does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definitions, or client SDKs; its GitHub organization (loft-br) hosts internal engineering and data-science tooling.

providers.name: Instil
providers.description: Instil is a purpose-built fundraising CRM and revenue-intelligence platform for nonprofit organizations, built for major-gifts and development teams. It manages the full donor lifecycle across major gifts, capital campaigns, planned giving, grant tracking, and moves management, and layers AI on top with One-Click Briefings that assemble a constituent's giving history and contact record on demand and Voice AI Logging that transcribes calls and writes interactions back to Instil or Salesforce. Instil connects to the nonprofit tech stack through Salesforce, Stripe, Classy, Mailchimp, Constant Contact, Eventbrite, Google, Outlook, and Zapier. It is backed by Threshold Ventures. No public developer API, documentation, or SDKs are published at this time; integrations are delivered through packaged connectors and Zapier.

providers.name: swivl
providers.description: swivl is an AI automation platform built specifically for the self-storage industry. It combines a unified CRM and contact center that consolidates calls, texts, emails, and chats with AI agents for sales, billing, support, and review management, plus a tenant mobile app (Spot) for access codes, payments, and referrals. Its self-storage natural-language model is trained on hundreds of thousands of customer conversations and serves 3,500+ locations. Founded in New York City and backed by Techstars, swivl advertises open APIs and integrations with major self-storage management systems, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: MHub
providers.description: MHub is a Malaysian property-technology (proptech) platform operated by TRB Ventures Sdn Bhd and backed by 500 Global. It gives real-estate developers an integrated system to manage the entire new-property sales cycle — from lead generation, launch, and online booking (Showroom, CRM, SalesCandy) through automated billing and collections (Credit Control), accounting and financial reporting, statutory compliance (HIMS/KPKT registry synchronization and LHDN-compliant e-invoicing), commission control, and handover/defect management. MHub runs a developer portal at developer.mhub.my and an authentication-gated REST API at api.mhub.my for platform integrations.

providers.name: Numero
providers.description: Numero is an all-in-one donor database and call-time platform built for political campaigns at the federal, state, and local levels. It combines a fast, filterable donor CRM with auto-deduplication and pledge tracking, a mobile call-time dialer with one-click SMS, email, and voicemail follow-up plus virtual local numbers, prefilled one-click contribution forms with access to a large 1-click donor network, event and RSVP fundraising tools, and a deliverability-focused email platform. Campaigns use Numero to identify prospect donors, run efficient candidate call time, and raise money faster. Numero is backed by Initialized Capital. It currently exposes no public developer API surface; api.numero.ai serves the web application backend only.

providers.name: Sankun
providers.description: Sankun (산군) is a South Korean construction-industry big data platform based in Seoul that aggregates and sells access to eight integrated construction databases covering roughly 280,000 construction companies, some 820,000 project sites, government e-procurement bids, contract awards, professional reputation reviews, and construction news. Alongside its web application and a construction sales CRM (Sankun Sales), the company markets a Sankun API (data.sankun.com) for programmatic access to its construction data, though public developer documentation is gated behind sales and login. Sankun is a portfolio company of 500 Global.

providers.name: Clubessential
providers.description: Clubessential is a Cincinnati-based provider of club management software for private country, golf, city, athletic, and yacht clubs. Its cloud suite unifies club websites and mobile apps, tee-time and dining reservations, membership CRM, point-of-sale, accounting, business intelligence, and integrated payments so club staff can manage operations and member experiences from a single platform. Part of Clubessential Holdings (unified under Xplor Technologies alongside ClubReady, foreUP, Vermont Systems, PrestoSports, and Exerp), the company serves more than 1,300 private clubs and, with its sister brands, thousands of courses and clubs worldwide. Backed by Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Item
providers.description: Item is an AI-native customer relationship management (CRM) platform, part of Y Combinator's Fall 2025 batch. It replaces the traditional CRM with an AI Assistant that handles daily work in plain language and customizable Agents that autonomously execute business processes across sales, support, and account management. Item connects to 100+ customer tools, gathers and enriches context automatically, discovers leads that match an ideal customer profile, and becomes a company's single source of truth for people, companies, and deals.

providers.name: Assemble
providers.description: Assemble builds autonomous AI agents that help enterprise IT and business-systems teams automate development work inside core platforms such as Salesforce, SAP, Workday, and NetSuite. The agents scope changes across integrated ERP, CRM, and HRIS systems, understand cross-system dependencies, implement and validate modifications, and keep a complete audit trail so teams can review agent work, approve modifications, and revert individual changes or restore a system to a prior state. Assemble is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) company targeting IT and business-systems teams managing complex enterprise transformations. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or OpenAPI, so only its verified public identity and website properties are captured.

providers.name: Hokan
providers.description: Hokan, Inc. (株式会社hokan) is a Japanese InsurTech company that builds hokan®, a cloud-based customer and contract management (CRM) system for insurance agencies and brokerages. The platform consolidates customer and policy information, digitizes proposal and activity workflows, and adds modules for intent capture (意向把握), case management (案件管理), dashboards, accounting/cashiering (出納), and staff management (People). It targets paperless operations, stronger audit and compliance controls, renewal and aftercare tracking, and mobile access for agents. Customers include Orix Life, ANA, Sekisui, and other Japanese insurers and agencies. Hokan is backed by 500 Global. The company exposes API-based website integration for its product but does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Salesape
providers.description: SalesAPE.ai (operated by AI AGENT GROUP LTD, a UK-registered company) builds AI sales assistants that automatically engage and qualify inbound leads across email, SMS, web chat, and WhatsApp. Its AI agents respond to prospects 24/7, qualify them, and book sales appointments so human teams focus on closing. SalesAPE connects to CRMs and automation tools including HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho, and Zapier (100+ integrations), logging and summarizing conversations back into the CRM. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass SalesAPE publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI; it exposes a customer app, a hosted status page, and standard legal pages. Sector: enterprise; AI.

providers.name: Branch8
providers.description: Branch8 is a digital solutions and managed contracting company headquartered in Hong Kong with operations across Asia (Singapore, Taiwan, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, and the Philippines). Founded in 2015, it provides managed technical squads and blended onshore/offshore teams that deliver e-commerce implementation (Adobe Commerce, Shopify Plus, and marketplace operations on Shopee, Lazada, and Amazon), CRM and CDP strategy (Salesforce, HubSpot, Segment, mParticle, Braze, Dynamics 365), digital product and mobile engineering, AI and workflow automation (n8n, Make, Windmill), and data engineering (Snowflake, BigQuery, dbt, Fivetran). Branch8 serves mid-market to enterprise clients including Chow Tai Fook, Chow Sang Sang, Lacoste, Hong Kong International Airport, Hotai/Toyota, and HKBN. It is a services firm rather than an API producer and publishes no public developer API, but it does expose an agent-native llms.txt describing its services.

providers.name: Avantos
providers.description: Avantos is an AI-native operating system for client management in financial services, built for wealth management and advisory firms. The platform unifies client data, products, teams, and workflows into a knowledge graph that powers agentic onboarding, relationship intelligence, and an AI-powered servicing workspace where agents anticipate client needs and streamline operations. It integrates with existing CRMs, custodians, and core systems, and is SOC 2 compliant with enterprise-grade architecture. Avantos raised a $35M Series A led by Bessemer Venture Partners, announced February 2026.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Widgera, Inc.
providers.description: Widgera is an AI-native business platform that unifies a company's operations into what it calls "One Adaptive OS." Its AI assistants (branded Aiva) learn a business, automate workflows, build internal apps, and run customer interactions across a suite of modules that includes CRM, Chats, Drive, Analytics, and autonomous Agents. Widgera positions itself as the infrastructure layer powering operations for retail, automotive, hospitality, real estate, and service organizations, with a roster of customers across consumer electronics retail, car service, real estate, and wellness. The company is backed by 500 Global. As of this profile Widgera runs a private application backend (api.widgera.com) but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; its public surface is a marketing site plus Privacy and Terms pages and homepage-published compliance posture (SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR).

providers.name: Superb
providers.description: Superb is a Denmark-based all-in-one Guest Experience Management (GXM) platform for restaurants, cafes and bars, bringing reservations, point of sale, payments, gift cards, online takeaway, guest CRM and marketing together in a single system. Superb does not publish a self-serve, documented public developer API. Guest bookings are taken through a hosted reservation widget, and third-party systems connect through Superb's catalog of pre-built connectors (accounting, payments, staff and stock management, marketing) plus a partner portal at partner.superbexperience.com. Any programmatic reservation, guest, booking or CRM access is partner-gated and arranged directly with Superb. The APIs listed below are logical capability groupings modeled from Superb's public product and help-center material - they are marked endpointsModeled because Superb does not publish endpoint-level REST documentation.

providers.name: Dinii
providers.description: Dinii (株式会社ダイニー) is a Tokyo-based restaurant-technology SaaS company, founded in June 2018, offering an "All in One Restaurant Cloud" for food-service businesses. Its integrated modules span POS register, customer mobile ordering, mobile self-checkout payment, customer management/CRM (with LINE integration), staff attendance and scheduling, reservation ledger, and management analytics dashboards (daily P&L, labor-cost optimization, QSC monitoring). Dinii reports 3,000+ installed locations and 20 million+ end users, with offices in Tokyo, Osaka, Sapporo, and Nagoya. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Dinii publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs at this time; this profile captures its identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Arzana
providers.description: Arzana is an AI-powered Office Execution System for US manufacturers and distributors, founded in 2025 in San Francisco and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026). Arzana trains custom models on a factory's historical data and deploys agents that automate back-office work — quoting, estimating, order entry, purchasing, prospecting, outreach, CRM, AP 3-way match, AR tracking, and customer service — alongside a customizable ERP/CRM/MES with every agent pre-installed. Forward-deployed engineers configure each agent per operation; Arzana reports going live in 120 days with 99%+ accuracy. Arzana currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; it does publish a /llms.txt for agent discovery.

providers.name: EAS Innovations Inc
providers.description: EAS Innovations Inc operates ELEV8, an end-to-end, cloud-based dealer management system (DMS) built for independent auto dealers and automotive finance companies. The platform unifies real-time accounting, inventory management, CRM and desking, loan servicing, payments and collections into a single fully-integrated system. It offers per-seat pricing, user-based access rights, user-level audit logs, whitelisted IP addresses, multi-rooftop access and department-level restrictions, and is delivered as a SaaS web application at app.elev8dms.com. EAS Innovations is a 500 Global portfolio company. No public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Breezy
providers.description: Breezy is a Los Angeles-based proptech startup building what it calls the first independent AI operating system for residential real estate. Founded in 2024 by top-producing agent James Harris alongside Afterpay co-founders Nick Molnar and Anthony Eisen, the mobile-first app consolidates an agent's workflow — comparable market analysis (comps), AI meeting notes, deal-pipeline management, client insights and an AI assistant — into a single workspace, and adds an "UnderBuilt Radar" that uses zoning, geospatial and setback data to flag properties with unrealized development potential across 1,200+ cities. Breezy raised a $10M pre-seed led by Ribbit Capital with participation from Fifth Wall, DST Global Partners, Liquid 2 Ventures, O.G. Venture Partners, Fidji Simo and David Marcus. The company exposes no public developer API today; this profile tracks it as a Fifth Wall portfolio lead.

providers.name: Dooly
providers.description: Dooly was a connected workspace for revenue teams that improved Salesforce CRM hygiene by syncing meeting notes, pipeline updates, and next steps back into Salesforce automatically. It layered a fast note-taking surface, deal vitals, real-time playbooks, and one-click CRM updates on top of Salesforce so account executives could keep their pipeline clean without manual data entry. Backed by Battery Ventures, Dooly was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. The Dooly platform was shut down on June 30, 2025; the company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal, and this profile captures the remaining public surface (website, privacy policy, terms) for the record.

providers.name: Buildertrend
providers.description: Buildertrend is an Omaha, Nebraska-based cloud construction-management platform serving residential home builders, remodelers, and specialty trade contractors. The product consolidates sales (CRM, leads, proposals, contracts, email marketing), project management (schedule, daily logs, selections, change orders, warranties, sub portal, client updates), and financial management (estimates, bids, takeoff, job-costing budgets, bills, purchase orders, invoices, online payments) into a single web and mobile application used by 20,000+ builders. Pricing is custom-quoted by sales rather than published self-serve tiers, with unlimited users and projects on every plan, and the platform integrates with QuickBooks, Xero, and other accounting and trade tools through a partner integrations marketplace. The company exposes a REST API at api.buildertrend.com that is gated by partner agreement — endpoints return 401 Unauthorized to the public and there is no open developer portal, public OpenAPI specification, or self-serve API key signup. As a result Buildertrend is profiled here as a non-public (partner-only) API provider; the public surface documented is limited to marketing, support, integrations marketplace, mobile apps, and corporate resources.

providers.name: Goomp Inc, Kalendar AI
providers.description: Kalendar AI (Goomp Inc / Kalendar Inc, a Delaware corporation operating from New York) is an autonomous AI sales-agent platform that automates B2B outbound prospecting end to end. It sources ideal-customer prospects from a database of hundreds of millions of professionals and companies, generates and sends personalized outreach through dedicated AI-managed mailbox infrastructure, qualifies replies, and books meetings directly onto the user's calendar. As of the 2026-08-13 enrichment pass the company has rebranded to Cockpit AI and migrated to oncockpit.ai — kalendar.ai now 301-redirects site-wide, and the new site's robots.txt carries an explicit "Block legacy Kalendar.ai paths" section. The product is now framed as named AI workers you "hire" (Vinay for outbound, Amara), which research prospects, draft proposal documents, send from the customer's own email and LinkedIn accounts, and book meetings, with a human approval step before anything ships. Investors named on the site are 500 Global, Boost VC, Asymmetry Ventures and Village Global. The company runs a live API host (api.oncockpit.ai, which self-identifies as the "Cockpit AI API") and still serves a legacy ChatGPT plugin manifest at /.well-known/ai-plugin.json declaring OAuth with read/write scopes, but it publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI, no SDK, no webhook catalog, no MCP server and no pricing page.

providers.name: Apparta
providers.description: Apparta is a Colombian hospitality technology company providing a reservation-management and guest-engagement platform for restaurants, bars, and dining venues across Latin America (Bogota, Medellin, Cali, Barranquilla). The SaaS product covers AI-assisted table assignment and floor-plan zoning, no-show prevention with prepayments and cancellation policies, a WhatsApp AI chatbot for automated bookings, CRM campaigns over SMS/email/WhatsApp, POS integration, branded booking pages and digital menus, and marketing connectors to Google, Google Maps, Instagram, TripAdvisor, and Facebook. Apparta is offered in tiered monthly plans (Basico, Standard, Plus) and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer API or OpenAPI surface is published as of this profiling; higher tiers expose a WhatsApp Business API integration on behalf of venues rather than a first-party Apparta API.

providers.name: KWI
providers.description: KWI is a retail technology company founded in 1985 and headquartered in Melville, New York, that delivers a cloud-based, unified commerce platform for specialty and department retailers. The platform combines an iOS mobile point-of-sale, merchandising and inventory optimization, order management with buy-anywhere / fulfill-from-anywhere fulfillment, CRM, clienteling and loyalty, the Snapshot real-time sales analytics application, and AI product image search, all operated as a SaaS managed service with helpdesk, hardware, and payments support. KWI describes an API layer in its platform architecture used to export data to third-party systems and channels --- CRMs, ERPs, SRPs, and supply chains --- alongside packaged connectors such as Shopify Connect and a Klaviyo connector. As of this profile KWI publishes no public developer portal, API reference, machine-readable specification, or SDKs; integration is delivered through its professional-services organization under customer contract.

providers.name: Altvia
providers.description: Altvia is fund management software purpose-built for private capital markets, serving private equity, venture capital, fund of funds, real estate, hedge funds, family offices, and placement agents. Built on the Salesforce platform, Altvia unifies a purpose-built CRM, a virtual data room (VDR) and LP investor portal, analytics and reporting, and an AI assistant (AIMe) into one system that spans the full fund lifecycle — capital raising, investor relations, and deal management. Founded in 2006 and based in Broomfield, Colorado, Altvia was acquired by Marlin Equity Partners in 2022. The company exposes no public developer/API portal; integrations are delivered through the platform and the Salesforce ecosystem.

providers.name: SAGARIS
providers.description: SAGARIS is an agentic revenue operating system for B2B sales teams — CRM, dialer, inbox, SMS, social, an AI receptionist and an AI coach in one system, where AI agents act on the pipeline under approval gates and an audit trail rather than only reporting on it. Pricing is public at 499 USD per founding seat per month, with a custom Enterprise plan. SAGARIS describes a Model Context Protocol endpoint that lets an AI client read the CRM, sequences and workspace with a workspace API key, read-only and scoped to the workspace.

providers.name: Personify
providers.description: Personify (Personify Inc., part of Momentive Software as of January 2026) is a constituent and association management software provider for associations, nonprofits, and member-based organizations. Founded in 1996 and headquartered in Austin, Texas, Personify offers a family of products - the enterprise Personify360 / ThreeSixty AMS, MemberClicks (MC Professional) for mid-sized professional and trade associations, Wild Apricot for small associations and clubs, and A2Z Events for event management. Several products expose documented REST APIs secured with OAuth 2.0. Wild Apricot and MemberClicks publish public developer documentation, while Personify360's Novus APIs (Swagger-documented) are provisioned through a customer's account manager. API access generally requires being a paying customer of the respective product.

providers.name: Chimelabs Holdings PTY LTD
providers.description: Chime Labs (Chimelabs Holdings PTY LTD) builds an AI voice receptionist and call-automation platform purpose-built for Australian trades and service businesses — plumbers, electricians, HVAC, locksmiths, pest control, cleaners and other on-the-tools operators. The AI answers missed inbound calls 24/7, qualifies and captures job details in natural Australian English, books work into scheduling and field-service systems (ServiceM8, Simpro, ServiceTitan, AroFlo, Fergus, Acuity Scheduling and Google Calendar), runs outbound calls, and turns quote calls into sent quotes automatically. Founded in 2025 in Sydney, Australia by Alexis Griveau (CEO) and Mathew Pretel and backed by 500 Global. The company operates a customer-facing SaaS product at platform.chimelabs.ai; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Cabal
providers.description: Cabal is an AI-powered relationship-intelligence and warm-introduction platform that turns an organization's professional relationships into warm introductions. It infers connections across millions of professional records without CSV uploads or calendar syncs, letting teams "ask who's connected to anyone." Cabal serves VC platform / deal-sourcing teams, sales organizations, and investor-relations and partnerships teams, and ships Cabal Mail for bulk personalized outreach (company updates, LP communications, strategic asks). The relationship graph is queryable through in-app chat, Claude and ChatGPT via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), a Slack bot, or an API. Backed by Craft Ventures. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Cabal's public surface; the company advertises API and MCP access but does not publish a public OpenAPI spec or open developer reference (both are account-gated).

providers.name: MoveitPro
providers.description: MoveitPro (MoveitPro+) is web-based moving company management software built by professional movers, covering the full operation of a moving and storage company - CRM and lead capture, estimating and quoting, a smart dispatch board with drag-and-drop scheduling and crew assignment, fleet and maintenance management, digital bills of lading and e-signatures, itemized inventory, storage and warehouse tracking, invoicing and credit-card payments, commission tracking, and AI call transcription and QA. MoveitPro advertises "Open API & Custom Integrations" and ships native integrations (QuickBooks, Twilio, Mailchimp, Google Maps/Calendar), but does not publish a self-serve public developer API, reference documentation, or OpenAPI. Its only publicly documented programmatic surface is a Zapier integration exposing Clients, Leads, Jobs, and Estimates. The APIs listed below are logical resources modeled from that documented Zapier integration; MoveitPro does not publish HTTP endpoints, base URLs, or authentication details.

providers.name: CloudCraze
providers.description: CloudCraze was an enterprise B2B commerce platform built natively on the Salesforce Platform, letting businesses launch online B2B storefronts fast and scale them on top of Salesforce CRM data. Brands including Coca-Cola, Cummins, Ecolab, Land O' Lakes, and WABCO ran global B2B commerce on it. Salesforce acquired CloudCraze in 2018 and folded it into the Salesforce B2B Commerce product line (now the legacy "B2B Commerce for Visualforce" managed package), where its Apex/JavaScript developer surface continues to be documented on Salesforce Developers. CloudCraze no longer operates as an independent company or developer portal — www.cloudcraze.com redirects to Salesforce B2B Commerce.

providers.name: Altitude Software
providers.description: Altitude Software is a contact center and unified customer interaction (uCI) software company founded in 1993 and headquartered in Lisbon, Portugal. Its flagship Altitude uCI suite provides omnichannel contact center capabilities — inbound/outbound campaigns, IVR and self-service, routing, dialer, recording and quality management, and CRM/ERP integration — with the Altitude uAgent SDK exposing Java, C/C++, .NET, SOAP, XML-RPC and web-service APIs for on-premises and cloud deployments. Altitude Software was a portfolio company of Insight Partners and was acquired by Enghouse Systems (TSX: ENGH) on 2020-12-30; the product line is now developed and maintained by Enghouse Interactive, and the brand continues to operate regionally (e.g. Altitude Software APAC). The company does not publish a modern public REST API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification; integration is delivered through the proprietary uAgent SDK and packaged CRM/ERP connectors.

providers.name: Atrium
providers.description: Atrium is a sales-effectiveness and sales-performance business intelligence platform for revenue teams. It continuously monitors sales KPIs to surface anomalies in rep and team performance, detects which behaviors and activities are driving (or dragging) output, and delivers AI-powered coaching recommendations to managers and reps. The product connects directly to Salesforce, HubSpot, data warehouses, and communication tools rather than exposing a public developer API. Founded in San Francisco by Jason Heidema (CEO) and Peter Kazanjy and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Bullpen Capital, and Electric Capital, Atrium was acquired by Fullcast in 2025 and is now offered as Fullcast Performance; atriumhq.com redirects to fullcast.com and only the customer application login at app.atriumhq.com remains on the Atrium domain.

providers.name: UnifiedCRM
providers.description: UnifiedCRM is a Seedcamp-backed startup (2023 investment) building a unified sales hub for remote and hybrid teams — an AI-assisted CRM delivered as a web app and PWA at unifiedcrm.ai, with features observed in the application such as email processing, deal summarization, contact and company enrichment, and automated web research. The company currently publishes no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: Awfar Market
providers.description: Awfar is a Cairo- and Riyadh-based digital solutions company (founded 2013) offering an integrated customer engagement and commerce platform. It combines an omnichannel Chat Center with AI agents (WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook), a cloud Call Center, and a Commerce & Delivery platform for order, inventory, and logistics management within a single interface. Awfar serves more than 2,000 clients across retail, pharmacy, restaurant, e-commerce, tourism, healthcare, education, and real estate, and ships prebuilt integrations for Shopify, Meta, Odoo, Zid, and Salla plus custom API connections. Backed by 500 Global. No public developer portal or OpenAPI specification is published at this time; integration is arranged via the sales and demo channel.

providers.name: Vymo
providers.description: Vymo is a sales-engagement and distribution-management platform for financial institutions — banks, insurers, and asset managers — helping field sales and collections teams manage leads, allocate and prioritize activities, and capture engagement in a mobile-first app. It layers AI-driven nudges, activity capture, and analytics on top of CRM and core systems, and integrates with existing enterprise ecosystems. Vymo does not publish a self-serve public developer API or documentation portal; its integrations are delivered through enterprise/partner connections. Backed by Emergence Capital and headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

providers.name: Placester
providers.description: Placester is a real estate marketing and technology platform that provides IDX-enabled websites, CRM, lead generation, and marketing automation tools for real estate agents, teams, and brokerages. Historically Placester published a developer-facing Real Estate API (api.placester.com) for listings, contacts, and website content, but the developer portal (developer.placester.com) now redirects to a site-unavailable page, indicating the public developer program is discontinued or inaccessible. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; no accessible public API surface, OpenAPI, or SDK was found at enrichment time.

providers.name: Agillion
providers.description: Agillion, Inc. was an Austin, Texas web-based customer relationship management (CRM) company founded in 1998 by Steve Papermaster. It offered small and mid-sized businesses a hosted, continuously updated online database that consolidated customer information as businesses and their customers interacted, an early software-as-a-service CRM offering. The company raised roughly $40M from investors including Cisco, Goldman Sachs, and Morgan Stanley and is carried as a portfolio company of Insight Partners. Agillion has since been permanently closed; its agillion.com domain no longer serves a website and the company exposes no public developer portal, documentation, or API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical record.

providers.name: AnswerSoft
providers.description: AnswerSoft, Inc. was a privately-held computer-telephony integration (CTI) software company based in Richardson, Texas. Its Concerto product line automated interactions between telephony systems and business applications, covering smart screen pop, intelligent call routing, data mining, and early internet-enabled call centers. Davox Corporation acquired AnswerSoft in a stock-for-stock transaction in 1998 to pair AnswerSoft's inter-application automation with Davox's Unison outbound call center line, taking the combined company into the emerging CRM market. Davox renamed itself Concerto Software in 2002, merged with Aspect Communications to form Aspect Software in 2005, and merged with Noble Systems to become Alvaria in 2021. AnswerSoft has not operated independently for over twenty-five years, publishes no API, developer program, or documentation, and the answersoft.com domain is now listed for sale on the GoDaddy aftermarket. This profile is retained as a historical acquired-company lead only.

providers.name: Baker Technologies
providers.description: Baker Technologies (Baker) was a Denver, Colorado based customer relationship management (CRM) and marketing platform built for the cannabis industry, founded in 2014 by David Champion, Joel Milton, and Roger Obando. A graduate of the 500 Startups accelerator, Baker helped licensed dispensaries grow revenue and build customer relationships through online ordering, loyalty programs, SMS/text messaging, and analytics, and launched an expanded integrations program with a developer API connecting dispensaries to 20+ ancillary cannabis services. The company raised approximately $11.75M (including an $8M Series A) before being acquired by TILT Holdings in 2018. The trybaker.com domain is now parked and listed for sale, indicating the product has been discontinued; no live developer portal, API documentation, or specifications are publicly available.

providers.name: Chordiant Software
providers.description: Chordiant Software Corporation was an enterprise software vendor founded in 1991 and based in California, known for customer relationship management (CRM) and customer decision management software used by large banks, insurers, telecommunications carriers, and healthcare organizations. Its products included Chordiant Decision Management, Marketing Director, and Recommendation Advisor, delivering real-time predictive decisioning and next-best-action recommendations across customer channels. The company went public on NASDAQ (CHRD) in 2000 and was acquired by Pegasystems in 2010, with its decisioning technology folded into Pega's Customer Decision Hub. Chordiant no longer operates as an independent company and exposes no public developer portal or API; the chordiant.com domain now redirects to pega.com. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record and carries no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Ciridae
providers.description: Ciridae is building an AI-native operating system for services businesses — the industrial, construction, and field-service companies that make up the real economy. Its platform replaces fragmented ERPs and spreadsheets with a unified system that automates core business operations across project management, financials, CRM, accounts payable and receivable, and reporting, while keeping humans in the loop to oversee AI decisions. Modules span AI-generated field workforce scheduling, vendor onboarding and compliance, automated payment workflows, and customer order expediting, typically deployed in a two-to-four-week implementation with embedded engineers. Founded in 2025 and based in San Francisco, Ciridae is backed by Accel. The company does not currently publish a public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Connected
providers.description: Connected (Connected HQ, Inc.) was a social CRM and contact-management startup that pulled a user's address book, email and social accounts together into a single continuously-updated relationship manager. Backed by 500 Global, it was acquired by LinkedIn in October 2011 and folded into the LinkedIn-branded "Connected" product, after which the standalone service was retired. Connected never shipped a public developer program, API, SDK or documentation. The connectedhq.com domain is still defensively held by the acquirer (MarkMonitor registrar, Azure DNS and NS1 nameservers, SPF and DMARC p=reject, RFC 7505 null MX) but publishes no A record and serves no content. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Consona
providers.description: Consona Corporation was an Indianapolis, Indiana enterprise software company founded in 1986 as Made2Manage Systems and taken private by Battery Ventures in 2003. Operating a roll-up strategy, it acquired multiple ERP and CRM product lines (DTR, Cimnet, AXIS, Encompix, Intuitive, Relevant, SupplyWorks) serving small and midsize manufacturers and field-service businesses. On August 7, 2012 Consona merged with CDC Software to form Aptean, and the Consona brand was retired from commercial use. The company is defunct, has no live web domain (consona.com does not resolve) and no public API or developer surface; its former products live on inside Aptean.

providers.name: Contactually
providers.description: Contactually was a cloud-based CRM (customer relationship management) platform focused on helping real estate agents, brokers, and other relationship-driven professionals nurture their networks through follow-up reminders, contact bucketing, pipelines, and automated outreach. Founded around 2011, it was acquired by real estate brokerage Compass on February 27, 2019, and had already been powering Compass's own CRM. Contactually permanently ceased operations on March 31, 2022. It historically exposed a v2 REST API (api.contactually.com) documented at developers.contactually.com for contacts, buckets, notes, tasks, and webhooks, but that developer surface, the API hosts, and all SDKs are now offline. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical record of a defunct provider; no live API, documentation, SDK, or event surface remains to enrich.

providers.name: Corio, Inc.
providers.description: Corio, Inc. was an enterprise Application Service Provider (ASP) founded in September 1998 in San Carlos, California, and incorporated in Delaware, formed by acquiring the capital stock of Data Systems Connectors, Inc. Corio implemented, hosted and managed packaged enterprise business software from Oracle, PeopleSoft, SAP, Ariba and Siebel Systems on behalf of medium and large public, private, non-profit and public sector customers, delivering ERP, CRM and e-business functionality as a service from secure third-party data centers over IP networks. The company operated two lines of business — Application Management Services and Professional Services — and partnered with (i)Structure, XO Communications and Qwest for data center and network infrastructure. Backed by Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers (29.5% pre-IPO across the KPCB Java Fund, KPCB VIII, KPCB VIII Founders Fund and KPCB Information Sciences Zaibatsu Fund II, with Vinod Khosla and Ted Schlein on the board) and Cap Gemini Ernst & Young, Corio went public on NASDAQ in 2000. IBM agreed to acquire Corio on 24 January 2005 for $2.82 per share in cash via Nike Acquisition Corp.; Corio filed its Form 15 deregistration on 15 March 2005 and was absorbed into IBM. The company is defunct, publishes no API, developer portal or documentation, and corio.com is a parked domain — there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Naranga
providers.description: Naranga is a cloud-based franchise management platform for franchisors and multi-location brands, covering franchise sales CRM and lead management (emaximation), operations and multi-location support (nCompass), employee and franchisee training (nSpire), field audits and inspections, task and job scheduling, and local/multi-channel marketing. API access model: Naranga does NOT publish a documented public or self-serve developer API. There is no developer portal, no published API reference, no OpenAPI/Swagger definition, no SDKs, and no self-serve API keys as of this entry. Integrations with third-party systems (for example Twilio, RingCentral, Microsoft 365, AssureSign, and lead-capture/Zapier-style connectors) exist but are delivered through Naranga's partner and professional-services onboarding (typically a multi-week implementation scoped per brand), not through open, documented, developer-facing endpoints. Pricing is quote-based / contact-sales.

providers.name: Node.io
providers.description: Node (Node.io, legally Node Inc.) was an artificial-intelligence startup founded in 2014 by former Google executive Falon Fatemi. Node marketed an "artificial intuition" platform that combined a customer's CRM data with a large external graph of people and companies to score and predict which prospects, partners, employees, or investors a business should engage next. The company raised roughly $16M from investors including 500 Global, Mark Cuban, Avalon Ventures, Canaan Partners, and Bee Partners. On 2020-08-24 Node Inc. was acquired by SugarCRM, which folded the technology into its sales and CX products rather than continuing to sell it as a standalone product. Node.io no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer portal, documentation, or public API; the node.io domain is now a parked GoDaddy/Afternic "for sale" listing. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record with no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: OneCommand
providers.description: OneCommand was a cloud-based customer marketing and loyalty-automation platform built for automotive dealerships, headquartered in Mason, Ohio. It helped dealers drive service and sales traffic, increase owner retention, and lower marketing costs through data-driven, multichannel outreach across voice, text, email, and direct mail. Its product family included the OneCommand loyalty-automation platform, the Higher Gear CRM, and the TrafficAccelerator service. OneCommand was absorbed into Affinitiv in September 2016, one of four automotive-marketing firms (with TimeHighway.com, Peak Performance and DPS) merged to form that company. The brand is now defunct as an operating surface — onecommand.com and portal.onecommand.com are still fronted by Cloudflare but the origin no longer answers (HTTP 522 on every path probed 2026-08-13), highergear.com no longer connects, and onecommand.net and trafficaccelerator.com resolve to parked landing pages. OneCommand never published a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation, and the acquirer's site (affinitiv.com) publishes none either.

providers.name: Parature
providers.description: Parature was a cloud-based customer service and self-service knowledge base company founded around 2000 (originally as Cyracle) and headquartered in Herndon, Virginia. Its SaaS suite covered a customer self-service knowledge base, ticketing/case management, live chat, and social customer service, and it exposed a developer API for managing knowledge base articles, tickets, and related data. Microsoft acquired Parature for a reported $100 million in January 2014 and folded its capabilities into Microsoft Dynamics CRM / Dynamics 365 for Customer Service. Parature from Microsoft stopped selling to new customers on November 1, 2016 and the standalone service was fully retired (end of support) on May 15, 2018. This is a historical/defunct company profile: the parature.com domain no longer resolves and there is no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Partnered
providers.description: Partnered was a cloud-based co-selling and partner-introductions platform that let sales teams request and exchange warm customer introductions with their partners' sales teams, enabling partner-powered co-selling at scale. Founded by Adam Michalski and Tim Sherwood and backed by Slow Ventures among other early investors, Partnered was acquired by Crossbeam on May 18, 2022, and its product was folded into Crossbeam's Ecosystem-Led Growth platform. The partnered.com domain now redirects to crossbeam.com; Partnered no longer operates as an independent company and exposes no independent public API surface.

providers.name: Rapportive
providers.description: Rapportive was a browser extension that added a contact-intelligence sidebar to Gmail, surfacing a person's name, photo, job, and social profiles alongside their email. Founded in 2011 and backed by 500 Global (then 500 Startups), it was acquired by LinkedIn in 2012 and later folded into LinkedIn Sales Navigator. The rapportive.com domain now 301-redirects to LinkedIn's "Sales Navigator for Gmail" feature page. Rapportive published no standalone developer API and operates no independent developer surface today; this profile records that defunct/absorbed status for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Soff
providers.description: Soff is an AI-powered quoting platform for U.S. distributors that turns inbound RFQs into won deals. It automatically captures requests for quotes from email, generates instant quotes and PDFs, tracks quote performance (won vs. lost), logs activity into ERP/CRM systems, and analyzes customer behavior and lost-deal reasons. Backed by Y Combinator (S24) and General Catalyst, based in San Francisco, and SOC 2 Type II certified. As of this enrichment pass Soff publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, or well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Vantus
providers.description: Vantus is a stub surfaced from the Mayfield portfolio page whose permalink slug is "vantus" but whose actual company is Vantive Corporation, a historic Mayfield "Milestone" enterprise investment described by Mayfield as call center software leaders. Vantive provided customer relationship management (CRM) software and existed as an independent corporation until its merger with PeopleSoft in 1999; PeopleSoft was later acquired by Oracle and the Vantive brand no longer exists. There is no current company website or API surface to enrich. Unrelated live domains (vantus.com, Vantus Medical Systems; vantus.io, a Spanish AI automation consultancy) are different companies and are intentionally not linked here.

providers.name: Vlocity
providers.description: Vlocity was an industry-cloud software company founded in 2014 (by David Schmaier and team) that built vertical CRM applications on the Salesforce Platform for communications, media, energy, insurance, health, and the public sector, along with the OmniStudio low-code toolset (OmniScript, FlexCards, DataRaptor, Integration Procedures). Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Accel, Sutter Hill Ventures, and Salesforce Ventures, Vlocity was acquired by Salesforce in 2020 and folded into Salesforce Industries; the platform now ships as Salesforce OmniStudio. Vlocity no longer exists as an independent company and publishes no independent developer portal or public API — its domain (vlocity.com) is defunct (HTTP 503) and is now operated by Salesforce (confirmed via SPF/DMARC delegation to salesforce.com and a Salesforce, Inc. TLS certificate). Any API surface lives under Salesforce OmniStudio.

providers.name: xchange (Formerly Exchange Applications Inc.)
providers.description: Xchange Inc., formerly Exchange Applications Inc., was a Boston-based (89 South Street, Boston, MA) customer relationship marketing software company that helped enterprises earn a greater share of their customers' business through relevant, personalized customer communications, selling campaign-management and customer-analytics software. A Delaware corporation backed by Insight Partners, it went public in 1998 (S-1 filed 1998-07-22, SEC CIK 0001065857, SIC 7373 Computer Integrated Systems Design). The company went dark after its final 10-Q on 2002-11-19, and the SEC revoked its Exchange Act registration on 2011-01-07. Both historical domains are now parked: xchange.com carries no A record and exchangeapplications.com is a domain-for-sale lander. The company is defunct with no website, developer surface, or APIs; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Sansan
providers.description: Sansan, Inc. is a Tokyo-based enterprise SaaS company that builds cloud contact- and business-card management software. Its flagship Sansan platform digitizes and centralizes business cards and customer contact data so sales teams can share information across the organization, surface opportunities, and integrate contact data with external systems. The company also offers the Eight business-card app and Bill One invoice-management product. As of this enrichment pass Sansan does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI definition on its English or Japanese websites; this profile captures the company identity and probed domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Givecampus
providers.description: GiveCampus is a digital-first fundraising and alumni-engagement platform built for educational institutions - K-12 schools, colleges, universities, and their affiliated foundations, alumni associations, and nonprofits. The platform provides online giving pages, Giving Days, crowdfunding and peer-to-peer (advocacy) fundraising, matching and challenge gifts, event and volunteer management, donor management and advancement CRM tooling, payment processing, and stewardship and engagement features that help advancement teams raise more money at a lower cost. Founded in 2015 and backed by Y Combinator, GiveCampus is used by thousands of schools and institutions across the United States and internationally. This API Evangelist profile tracks GiveCampus as a company in the network; the company operates a closed SaaS product and does not publish a public developer API, so this record is identity- and infrastructure-focused.

providers.name: Lumific
providers.description: Lumific is a client reactivation platform for med spas that reconnects dormant clients with a practice to recover revenue from high-value treatments. Its proprietary system identifies inactive clients in an existing CRM (such as Mindbody or Zenoti) and launches automated, multi-channel outreach campaigns combining personalized text messaging, professional phone calls, and instant gift-card offers to drive bookings. Campaigns launch within 24 hours, pricing is performance-based (commission only on completed treatments), and the service is TCPA and HIPAA compliant with market exclusivity limited to a few clinics per area. Lumific was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. This provider currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Seneca Systems
providers.description: Seneca Systems is a govtech company whose stated mission is "building better government" through software that helps public-sector organizations serve constituents and modernize internal operations. Its flagship product is Romulus, a constituent-relationship and case-management platform aimed at local and state government. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Cowboy Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable discovery surface.

providers.name: Tact.ai
providers.description: Tact.ai was a Redwood City, California conversational-AI and field-engagement company founded by Chuck Ganapathi that built an AI sales assistant ("Tact Assistant") unifying CRM, email, and calendar data into a voice- and chat-driven interface for enterprise sales teams, later concentrating on the life sciences vertical. It was backed by Accel, Redpoint Ventures, Upfront Ventures, Microsoft's M12, and Salesforce Ventures. In November 2023 its field-engagement and conversational-AI technology was acquired by Aktana and the standalone company wound down. The tact.ai domain no longer hosts a product: it resolves to an Afternic domain-for-sale parking page (nameservers ns1/ns2.afternic.com), and the company exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal to enrich.

providers.name: Banksight
providers.description: BankSight Systems is a cloud banking software company founded in 2015 (San Francisco / Mumbai) that built an intelligent banking CRM and customer engagement platform for community banks, regional banks, and credit unions. The platform consolidated and analyzed customer data on top of Microsoft Azure and the Microsoft Power Platform, running a banking-specific data model with an open integration framework of pre-built connectors to core, LOS, and legacy banking systems, and delivered AI-driven "Next Best Conversation" recommendations to bankers and wealth managers. BankSight was acquired by Bottomline Technologies; its product now lives inside Bottomline's Commercial Digital Banking platform, and banksight.com 301-redirects to bottomline.com. This profile was surfaced as a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company (since exited) and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.
